answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can earn rewards. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, so a Sybil flood drains the attacker's own capital instead of printing free influence. Honest agents get their stake back with earnings, while proven cheaters lose theirs, and the penalty sends a ripple through the whole river of rewards: each lost stake raises the price of the next fake identity, keeping the network's pulse healthy only when identities cost more to fake than they return.
